facts.text: A wheel loader is a four-wheeled machine with a large front bucket that scoops up loose material and tips it into a truck or onto a pile.
facts.quote: A wheel loader is a four-wheeled machine with a large bucket at the front that scoops up loose material and tips it into a truck or onto a pile.

facts.text: In the United States, a wheel loader is also called a front-end loader.
facts.quote: In the United States the same machine is called a front-end loader.

facts.text: Wheel-loader work involves short forward and reverse moves with people, trucks and piles close by.
facts.quote: Its day is spent in short forward and reverse moves with people, trucks and piles close by.

facts.text: In US surface-mine fatality reports from 2000 to mid-2006, front-end loaders were involved in 33% of 22 blind-area deaths, second only to dump trucks.
facts.quote: in US surface-mine fatality reports from 2000 to mid-2006, front-end loaders were involved in 33% of 22 blind-area deaths, second only to dump trucks [Chapter 4].

facts.text: The first commercial automatic braking on earth-moving machines was fitted to wheel loaders; the passage characterizes all such braking as narrowly scoped.
facts.quote: The first commercial automatic braking on earth-moving machines was fitted to wheel loaders, and all of it is narrow.

facts.text: Volvo CE's wheel-loader automatic braking system, dated January 2023, brakes only in reverse, between 3 and 15 km/h, for 2 to 3 seconds.
facts.quote: Volvo CE's system (January 2023) brakes only in reverse, between 3 and 15 km/h, for 2 to 3 seconds

facts.text: Volvo CE's wheel-loader automatic braking system remembers the last slope climbed so that reversing down a stockpile does not trigger braking.
facts.quote: remembers the last slope climbed so that reversing down a stockpile does not trigger it.

facts.text: Caterpillar's and Liebherr's wheel-loader automatic braking systems act only in reverse.
facts.quote: Caterpillar's and Liebherr's loader systems also act in reverse only.

facts.text: Neither Volvo CE, Caterpillar nor Liebherr publishes weather limits, false-intervention rates or validation methods for the wheel-loader braking systems described in the passage.
facts.quote: None publishes weather limits, false-intervention rates or validation methods [Chapter 2].

facts.text: The booklet identifies the wheel loader as the clearest case of a machine whose normal work looks like a collision risk to a sensor, making wheel loaders the hardest place to avoid nuisance braking.
facts.quote: The wheel loader is the clearest case of a machine whose normal job is also what a sensor sees as a collision risk, so it is the hardest place to avoid nuisance braking.

facts.text: Every fielded off-road braking product launched on wheel loaders with reverse-only, low-speed operation.
facts.quote: Every fielded off-road braking product launched on loaders in reverse only at low speed

facts.text: The booklet expects the collision-mitigation program to follow the narrow operating domain of reverse-only, low-speed wheel-loader braking.
facts.quote: in reverse only at low speed, the narrow operating domain the booklet expects this program to follow [Chapters 1, 2].
